rows.asks: What do the surfaces of this group mean, as the dictionary gives their meaning? State the one meaning, or the one kind of meaning, they share, in words the Strong's meaning of their codes supports; the group is named for it.

evidence.verse: For to set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace.
For to set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace.
For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit.
But turning and seeing his disciples, he rebuked Peter and said, “ Get behind me, Satan! For you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of man.”

fill.obs_text: The surfaces of this group, mind on, minds on and setting your mind, share one kind of meaning in the dictionary: the mind's set or direction, a frame of thought directed to something. G5427 gives purpose, frame of thought, will and aspirations, and G5426 gives to think, to set one's mind on, to have a certain attitude. The three surfaces are the noun and the verb of one root and stand in two verses, Rom 8:5-6 and Mar 8:33, where the mind is set on the flesh or the Spirit, or on the things of God or of men.
